Header:
Date: 2025-02-10 14:00 EST | Duration: 42m | Recording ID: ff-20250210-arcadia-quickstart-001
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), David Lin (Arcadia CTO), Marta Gomez (Product Lead), Omar Reyes (Infra)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on Arcadia's plan to add AI-assisted product recommendations and internal search. Main interest: quick self-serve evaluation of Redwood hosted API (time-to-first-token, free credits) with an eye toward Dedicated later for compliance. Discussed integration surface, security (SOC2, KMS), and initial perf expectations. Next: Sandbox + perf POC.

Topics:
- Quickstart path and free credits
- Time-to-first-token and SDKs
- Data residency / private deployment questions
- Typical Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs (cost, latency, isolation)
- Benchmark/POC plan and timeline

- see metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Morgan (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm alex from redwood, i'm the account lead here. priya my solutions eng will walk through the quickstart experience and answer any perf questions.
[00:12] David Lin (Arcadia): hey thanks - david here. we're curious mostly about how fast we can get tokens out, like, time to first token, and how the hosted quickstart works with our privacy constraints.
[00:22] Priya Shah (SE): yep, makes sense. welcome. high level, the hosted api is designed for really quick time-to-first-token — sign up, claim free credits, spin a key, and you can be calling in a few minutes. with our sdk we usually see teams get to a functioning request in under five minutes; if you do a curl it's basically instantaneous aside from the typical network latency.
[00:40] Marta Gomez (Arcadia): when you say "free credits", is that like a trial account that expires? and is usage isolated from other customers?
[00:49] Alex Morgan: good q. free credits are account-level promotional credits you redeem in the console, they let you call hosted models without billing until credits are exhausted or the promo period ends. usage is isolated by account and api key; we don't mix telemetry across accounts.
[01:02] Omar Reyes (Arcadia): and for security — does the hosted option give us audit logs and SSO? our infra team needs SAML + audit trails for any external service.
[01:11] Priya Shah: yes, hosted has an enterprise plan that includes SSO (SAML/Okta), detailed request-level audit logs, and you can enable KMS integration for encrypting model payloads at rest. for stricter controls you can move to Dedicated or Private which gives VPC peering / private network connectivity.
[01:27] David Lin: if we wanted to evaluate latency, what's the usual path? i.e., do we run a perf POC on hosted first or jump to dedicated?
[01:35] Priya Shah: typical flow is hosted quickstart to validate functionality and prompt design, then a short performance POC on Dedicated if you care about consistent tail latency and throughput. hosted is great to validate and iterate because it's fast to start; Dedicated gives predictable tps with reserved capacity and stricter isolation.
[01:50] Alex Morgan: and we can also run a short benchmarking script from your region against our hosted nodes to give you a baseline median/95/99 numbers before committing to Dedicated.
[02:00] Marta Gomez: can you give ballpark numbers? we care about 95th percentile latency under 500ms for interactive recs at 256 tokens.
[02:08] Priya Shah: ballpark — depends on model and sequence length. for a mid-size open model on hosted we often see median first-token in 80-200ms and 95th under 600ms in US regions, but it depends on queueing and your burst profile. Dedicated can tighten that to sub-300ms 95th for similar model families with the right pool sizing.
[02:28] David Lin: ok. also curious about costs — how do you recommend we estimate cost during the POC?
[02:33] Alex Morgan: we'll send a simple cost worksheet — tokens in/out plus model unit cost, and recommended batching/caching knobs. Redwood Optimize suggestions can reduce unit cost by up to ~30% for typical workloads by batching and KV caching.
[02:46] Omar Reyes: there's a point i want to clarify — we have to keep certain logs within our region for compliance. does hosted support regional data residency?
[02:55] Priya Shah: yes, we have region controls; hosted can route requests to specific regions depending on account settings. for strict residency we usually recommend Dedicated in a specific cloud region or Private for on-prem.
[03:08] Marta Gomez: about the quickstart — what do you include? any sample prompts or reference app we can fork?
[03:14] Alex Morgan: we have quickstart templates: example curl, node/python SDK, and a small reference app for product recommendations. we'll drop links — the repo has a lightweight frontend + server that demonstrates prompting patterns and fallback logic.
[03:24] David Lin: perfect. how good are the SDKs? we have a node backend.
[03:28] Priya Shah: node and python are first-class, with streaming support, function calling helpers, and examples for structured outputs. sometimes the auto-transcripts mislabel functions, ha — but basically you can stream responses with a single npm install and a few lines.
[03:41] Alex Morgan: quick note on time-to-first-token — for new accounts there's an activation step that takes a minute or two (email/SMS verification depending on plan). once activated, the key works right away. if you want an even faster path for the team we'll pre-provision a sandbox key and share it.
[03:57] Marta Gomez: i'd like that, yes. can we get a key scoped to just a particular model so it's limited?
[04:02] Priya Shah: yep, API keys can be scoped by model and by rate limit. we can issue short-lived keys for the POC.
[04:09] David Lin: regarding private deployment — we might need an on-prem option for certain stores with PII. what's involved in that transition?
[04:17] Priya Shah: Private is more involved: deploy our runtime behind your VPC or on-prem cluster. you'll get a private control plane and we hand over an enterprise package. typical lead time is weeks to months depending on network setup and compliance reviews. we provide an installer and support the KMS/HSM integrations.
[04:33] Omar Reyes: do you support air-gapped installs?
[04:35] Priya Shah: yes, we have an air-gap package for very regulated customers; it's one of the reasons customers choose Private over Dedicated.
[04:41] Alex Morgan: i want to tee up a small hosted exercise first: we give you credits, you redeem in console, we provision a scoped api key, and you run 1-2 example prompts and the small benchmark script. priya will send the exact commands.
[04:53] Marta Gomez: good. what about model versions? we want to pin to a model for consistency during the POC.
[04:59] Priya Shah: you can pin model versions in the api call; we have a catalog with redwood-verified tags and you can request a specific sha/version. rollouts are supported if you later want to test variants.
[05:10] David Lin: any gotchas with tokenization differences if we migrate models? we use token-level cost metrics internally.
[05:16] Priya Shah: tokenization will vary by model family; in our cost worksheet we include tokens-per-prompt estimates for recommended models. when you switch models there's a token delta to account for, we'll help you measure that in the POC.
[05:26] Omar Reyes: networking — for Dedicated we need to know if we can do VPC peering into our VPC, or if it's just private subnets in your cloud.
[05:33] Priya Shah: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints depending on cloud provider. we'll collect your network CIDRs in the next step and run a network readiness checklist.
[05:43] Alex Morgan: ok let's dig quick into the perf measurement priya mentioned — what do we need from arcadia to run a short hosted baseline?
[05:50] Priya Shah: we'll need a representative prompt set (5-10 prompts), expected concurrency pattern (rps) and desired sequence length. we'll provide a small benchmark harness that runs requests with realistic timing and reports median/95/99 latencies.
[06:04] David Lin: we can share the prompt set. target rps is small — peaky during spikes, maybe 50 rps sustained for a minute and burst to 200.
[06:13] Priya Shah: great, that'll be sufficient for a hosted baseline. for Dedicated sizing we'll translate that into GPU pool sizing and expected tps.
[06:20] Marta Gomez: one more on compliance — is there an SOC2 report we can review?
[06:24] Alex Morgan: yes, we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs. there's also a security whitepaper and an architecture diagram we can include.
[06:32] David Lin: i appreciate that. do you have references in retail or recommender systems?
[06:37] Alex Morgan: we do — a couple of e-comm customers using Redwood for on-site recs and search. i'll anonymize and share case notes.
[06:44] Omar Reyes: can the quickstart show streaming tokens? that's important for our UX.
[06:48] Priya Shah: yes, the reference app demonstrates streaming in the browser and server. streaming latency is typically lower for token start, and you can render partial outputs.
[06:57] Marta Gomez: any obvious red flags we should watch for during eval?
[07:00] Priya Shah: watch for tokenization surprises and prompt latency under your real network conditions; also look at 95/99 tail behavior — what looks fine at median can hide spikes. we'll help instrument metrics into your dashboard.
[07:12] Alex Morgan: ok wrapping — next steps: i'll send the quickstart + free credit redemption and scoped key, priya will send benchmark script and perf POC runbook, david you'll share prompts and compliance notes. we agreed to aim for a POC kickoff the week of 2025-02-24.
[07:28] David Lin: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:31] Marta Gomez: thanks.
[07:33] Alex Morgan: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the calendar invite.

Note: transcript contains a few misheard words and abbreviations typical of automated transcription (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, occasional speaker label swaps).
